A class with a `toJSON()` method serializes its result instead of its own fields, matching JS — same override dispatch as `toString()`. Under `-compat=strict` a heterogeneous array is rejected with an actionable error naming the escape hatches — a fixed-length **tuple** (`[number, string, boolean]`, which stringifies correctly), an explicit `any[]` annotation, or `-compat=js`

A *statically-typed* object/array *value* (not a literal) boxed into an element is type-erased, so deep `JSON.stringify` of it throws the clean "statically-typed value in a dynamic position" TypeError — the [TDD-00200](../tdd/TDD-00200.md) nested-value boundary

Type-directed projection off the parse tree ([TDD-00077](../tdd/TDD-00077.md)/[ADR-00224](../adr/ADR-00224.md)): nested objects, array-typed fields, and object-array fields (`Item[]`) all project through one path. A nullable-scalar field keeps its null-vs-value boxing; a missing field falls back to its type's default

caveats: A bare reassignment into a **member or element** target (`obj.items = JSON.parse(...)`, `grid[i] = JSON.parse(...)`) isn't projected from declaration context — but writing the target type on the call (`obj.items = JSON.parse(...) as Item[]`) projects anywhere ([ADR-00715](../adr/ADR-00715.md)); a typed var-decl and a declared-variable reassignment (`let xs: T[] = …; xs = JSON.parse(...)`) both project ([ADR-00571](../adr/ADR-00571.md))
notes: Projects the tree's array node into the standard `{ptr,i64}` aggregate, reusing the array-literal build path ([ADR-00224](../adr/ADR-00224.md))

A reassignment `xs = JSON.parse(s)` / `obj = await res.json()` into an array- or object-typed **variable** projects against the binding's declared type, the same as a typed var-decl ([ADR-00571](../adr/ADR-00571.md))

caveats: The `SyntaxError` message is position-based (`Unexpected token in JSON at position N`), not Node/V8's exact per-token wording
notes: A real recursive-descent parser ([TDD-00077](../tdd/TDD-00077.md)/[ADR-00223](../adr/ADR-00223.md)) (embedded C, `__kml_json_*` ABI) builds+validates a tagged value tree. Strict JSON (double quotes, no trailing commas/leading zeros/trailing junk), `\uXXXX`+surrogate decoding, a 512-deep runtime depth guard on untrusted input. `Response.json()` inherits it

caveats: The result is a dynamic tree — statically-typed operations on it (arithmetic on elements, passing into typed slots) hit the normal `any` limits until narrowed; `JSON.parse(s) as T` narrows at the source, routing through the typed projection instead ([ADR-00715](../adr/ADR-00715.md))
notes: Untyped/`any`-annotated `JSON.parse` keeps the whole tree as dynamic values ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md) Stage 2, [ADR-00622](../adr/ADR-00622.md)): objects become runtime property bags, arrays dynamic arrays (`.length`, index reads/writes with JS extension semantics, `for...in`), scalars their runtime tags — `data.server.ports[0]` just works. A bare `const data = JSON.parse(s)` with no annotation is this dynamic parse, matching JS

`JSON.stringify` serializes a dynamic tree back (round-trip clean): undefined values skipped in objects / `null` in arrays, NaN/Infinity → `null`, cycles throw `Converting circular structure to JSON`. The `space` argument pretty-prints a dynamic value byte-identically to the static path and to Node ([TDD-00077](../tdd/TDD-00077.md) P4, [ADR-00639](../adr/ADR-00639.md)); a nested array literal inside an `any`-typed object literal recurses into a dynamic array, so it is navigable and serializable
